issues.display_title: Issue #1406: Auto Level: optimize output file size (quality setting / no bloat)
issues.main_description_html:
Split from #1403 (tracker). Sibling task: #1407 (slow save).

Result

Video

In the previous generation result, the file size doubled, increasing from 12MB to 24MB. The latest update resolves this by upgrading the binary, resulting in much better file size efficiency. The output size is now consistently within ±2MB of the original file size

Problem (from #1403)

The newly implemented Auto Level feature is working, but it has introduced significant issues during the image processing and saving phase. This task covers File Size Bloat:

File Size Bloat (Quality Setting)

Processed images are increasing drastically in size (e.g., from an original 17MB up to 29MB). This indicates the image processing engine might be exporting/saving the JPEG at 100% quality instead of matching the original file's compression level or using a sensible default (e.g., 85%–90%).

Acceptance Criteria

  1. Optimized File Size: The output file size of an auto-leveled image is roughly equivalent to the input file size (no 100% quality bloat).
  2. Output remains a valid, viewable 360° image with correct horizon; metadata (GPS, GPano/XMP, camera) preserved.

Root cause & approach

pano-level is spawned with only --input/--output (src/main/functions/AutoLevel/panoLevel.ts:103) and re-encodes the equirect at its own near-lossless default. The binary exposes no JPEG quality flag → size must be controlled via post-processing. Reuse the existing gtminify --quality Q binary (src/main/functions/MinifyJpg/minifyJpg.ts:88). New pipeline order: pano-level → gtminify --quality Q → copyMetadata.

Subtasks

  • A0 — Measure: benchmark in/out bytes on 3–5 samples at Q=85/90; record numbers in docs/brainstorm/planning.md §2.
  • A1 — No-op skip: if dry-run roll/pitch within ~0.1° deadband, copy source instead of re-encoding; show "already level" in UI.
  • A2 — Wire gtminify into the AutoLevel path, compressing output in-place before copyMetadata (panoLevel.ts:136-139).
  • A3 — Settings + plumbing: add { compress, quality } to StartConfigAutoLevel (autoLevelQueueManager.ts:15), Redux editReducer, AutoLevel/Settings.tsx, preload signatures. Default quality ≥85, opt-in. Consider Original/Web/Print presets.
  • A4 — Verify metadata survives the extra encode (TC1, TC2).

Risk

Double JPEG encode compounds quality loss → keep quality conservative (≥85) and compression opt-in.

Testing Scenario (for Tester)

Pre-conditions: App build with the fix installed · at least one tester machine (note CPU/RAM) · sample images ready. Record the input file size of every sample before testing.

Test data to prepare:

  • A normal, slightly-tilted equirectangular 360° JPG (e.g. a ~17MB, 2:1 ratio panorama) — the main "happy path".
  • A non-panorama image and a non-JPG file — for negative checks.

TC1 — Output File Size (AC #1)

  1. Open Edit → Auto Level, add the normal 17MB panorama to the queue.
  2. Apply / run Auto Level and let it finish (Status = Success).
  3. Locate the output file and check its size.
  4. Expected: Output size is roughly equivalent to the input (not drastically larger — no jump to ~29MB / 100% quality). Output remains a valid, viewable 360° image with correct horizon.

TC2 — Metadata Preserved (regression for AC #1)

  1. Using the TC1 output, open file info / EXIF.
  2. Expected: GPS, GPano/XMP, and camera metadata are preserved from the source; image is still recognized as a 360° panorama.

TC7 — Output Mode Regression

  1. Test both overwrite source and Create New File modes.
  2. Expected: Output lands in the correct location; size/quality behaves the same in both modes; existing queue controls (Remove, Cancel, Stop All, Clear Completed, View output) still work.

Reference

docs/brainstorm/planning.md §2 · docs/brainstorm/brainstorming.md Issue 1 · docs/brainstorm/analyze.md §5a.

issues.display_title: Issue #1407: Auto Level: fix slow save time (ExifTool singleton, redundant reads, queue)
issues.main_description_html:
Split from #1403 (tracker). Sibling task: #1406 (file size bloat).

Result

Video

Macos

before:

after:

As shown in the media above, the generation process is now 96% faster, dropping from ~16s to ~2s. This significant improvement is achieved by utilizing a cutting-edge plugin that greatly accelerates the image generation process.

Problem (from #1403)

The newly implemented Auto Level feature is working, but it has introduced significant issues during the image processing and saving phase. This task covers Performance / Slow Saving:

Performance / Slow Saving

The process of saving the auto-leveled image is taking an excessively long time ("took forever").

Acceptance Criteria

  1. Acceptable Processing Time: The image saves within a reasonable timeframe (e.g., under 5–10 seconds depending on resolution); no indefinite "took forever" hang.
  2. Progress UI updates and completes; Stop/Cancel stays responsive; one slow/failed item does not block the others.

Root causes (multiple)

  1. Per-file ExifTool churn — copyMetadata does new ExifToolClass(...) then .end() for every file (src/main/functions/copyMetadata.ts:387 / :410); a singleton (getExifToolSingleton) already exists but is unused here.
  2. Redundant GPS read — a second exiftool.read() of the destination in updateGPSDatabase (copyMetadata.ts:329).
  3. Strictly sequential queue — processNext() recurses one file at a time (src/main/functions/AutoLevel/autoLevelQueueManager.ts:178), single AbortController.
  4. Fake progress — jumps 30 → 100 (autoLevelQueueManager.ts:135), so "slow" also feels worse.

Subtasks (phased by risk)

  • B1 — ExifTool singleton reuse (quick win, no UX change): swap per-file new ExifTool/.end() for getExifToolSingleton(); confirm shared lifecycle isn't .end()-ed mid-batch.
  • B2 — Drop redundant GPS read: reuse source metadata already read; verify GPS DB correctness.
  • B3 — Honest progress milestones: replace fake 30→100 with analyze → encode → metadata.
  • B4 — Bounded parallel queue: K = min(cpu-1, 3–4) workers, one AbortController each, preserving per-item cancel + global stop. Cap total concurrent native processes (pano-level + gtminify + exiftool) — interacts with #1406 compression.

Risk

Parallelism + large equirects = memory pressure; cancel/stop semantics must stay correct after the refactor.

Testing Scenario (for Tester)

Pre-conditions: App build with the fix installed · at least one tester machine (note CPU/RAM) · sample images ready.

Test data to prepare:

  • A large/high-resolution equirectangular JPG (e.g. ≥ 20–30MB) — for the performance check.
  • A batch of several normal panoramas — for throughput / resilience.

TC3 — Processing / Save Time (AC #1)

  1. Add the large/high-res panorama to the queue and run Auto Level. Time from Apply → Success.
  2. Repeat with a batch of several images.
  3. Expected: Each image saves within a reasonable timeframe (≈ under 5–10s per image depending on resolution); no indefinite "took forever" hang. Progress UI updates and completes; Stop/Cancel still responsive.

TC5 — Mixed Batch / Resilience

  1. Queue a mix of several images (incl. at least one that fails) and run.
  2. Expected: Normal images succeed; a failing item fails gracefully; one failure does not block or fail the others.

Reference

docs/brainstorm/planning.md §3 · docs/brainstorm/brainstorming.md Issue 2 · docs/brainstorm/analyze.md §5a.

issues.display_title: Issue #1403: Handle Issue Auto Level Output Bloat, Slow Save Time, and "Correction Too Large" Error
issues.main_description_html:
This task has been split into sub-issues and now serves as a tracker. Each problem is tracked and tested independently below.

The newly implemented Auto Level feature (Edit → Auto Level) is working, but it introduced issues during the image processing and saving phase. The work has been split:

Sub-issueProblemAcceptance
#1406File Size Bloat (Quality Setting) — output JPEG much larger than input (e.g. 17MB → 29MB).Output ≈ input size, no 100% quality bloat.
#1407Performance / Slow Saving — saving takes "forever".Saves in ~under 5–10s; no hang; responsive cancel.

Each sub-issue carries the full problem statement, acceptance criteria, root-cause analysis, subtasks, and its testing scenario (TC1/TC2/TC7 → #1406, TC3/TC5 → #1407).

The third original concern — Unhandled JSON Error (correction_too_large) — was tracked in #1408 but has been canceled.

Reference / Investigation

Root-cause analysis and solution options live in the brainstorming docs (branch brainstorming):

  • docs/brainstorm/brainstorming.md — divergent solution options per issue.
  • docs/brainstorm/planning.md — converged decisions, phasing, and acceptance/verification.
  • docs/brainstorm/analyze.md §5a — AutoLevel pipeline context.
